chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Al-Fudayl bin Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman for a thousand dirhams, so he gave her a fugitive slave of his and a garment, a veil, valued at the thousand dirhams which was her dower. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she is pleased with the slave, and she had known him, there is no problem when she takes possession of the garment and is pleased with the slave.' I said, 'And if he divorces her before he enters with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dower for her, and she returns to him five hundred dirhams, and the slave is for her.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the dower if a man divorces his wife before consummation when the dower includes both money and goods?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the application of the 'half dower' rule in Surah Al-Baqarah when the dower consists of mixed assets, establishing that the wife retains the specific item accepted as part of the settlement (the slave) while returning half the liquid value. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that acceptance of specific goods validates their retention as part of the dower share, distinguishing between consumable cash and durable assets. This ruling underscores the importance of mutual consent (rida) in the composition of the mahr and its subsequent division upon pre-consummation divorce.
